problem:
Given that $x,y\in {C}^{3},$ compute the standard Hermitian inner product $⟨x,y⟩$ of the following two vectors.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}1+i \\ 2 \\ 2-i\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}1+i \\ 3 \\ 2+i\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem:
Given that $x,y\in {C}^{3},$ compute the standard Hermitian inner product $⟨x,y⟩$ of the following two vectors.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}1-4\text{i} \\ 1-6\text{i} \\ \text{i}\end{aligned}],\,y=[\begin{aligned}\text{i}+4 \\ \text{i}+9 \\ -\text{i}\end{aligned}].
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
Using the definition of the standard Hermitian inner product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & ={x}_{1}\overset{―}{{y}_{1}}+{x}_{2}\overset{―}{{y}_{2}}+{x}_{3}\overset{―}{{y}_{3}} \\  & =(1-4i)\cdot (\overset{―}{i+4})+(1-6i)\cdot (\overset{―}{i+9})+\text{i}\cdot (\overset{―}{-\text{i}}) \\  & =(1-4i)\cdot (4-i)+(1-6i)\cdot (9-i)+\text{i}\cdot \text{i} \\  & =(-17i)+(3-55i)+(-1) \\  & =2-72i.\end{aligned}
$$
